THE MYSTERY
FILES.

Hear the clues. Read the story. Solve the cases. Create your own mystery.

🗣 Speaking📖 Reading🧠 Used to / Past Simple🧩 Missions
01
Warm-up · 4 min

What happened last night?

Imagine you heard a strange noise in this room. What could it be?

🎤 Talk like a detective

Make three guesses. Then explain your favourite theory.

“I think it was… because…”

“Maybe somebody…”

“As soon as I heard the noise, I…”

Accept all logical explanations. Encourage a reason with because and a past-time sentence.
02
Looking back · 7 min

Story Detective

Quick recall · Choose the genre

🎙 30-second story

Invent a book using these four elements:

Genre → Character → Place → Problem

Use two Past Simple verbs.

“An intelligent detective went to an old castle. She found…”
00:30
Possible genres: science fiction, mystery, adventure, comedy. Transition: What makes a story mysterious?
03
Vocabulary discovery · 7 min

Sound Detective Board

Which sounds can people make? Which sounds can nature make?

🔍 Match meaning to word

whisper, gasp, sigh, snore, gust of wind, laugh. Gasp and whisper can also be nouns.
04
Controlled practice · 5 min

Complete the scene

WORD BANK: gust · whisper · gasp · snore · scared · laugh
1 gust, 2 whisper, 3 gasp, 4 snore, 5 scared, 6 laugh.

🎭 Make it real

Choose two completed sentences. Act them out or make a new mini-scene with your teacher.

“A gust of wind opened the window. I heard a whisper and felt scared.”
05
Pre-reading · 4 min

The Silver Box

An old castle. An open window. A missing silver box. A strange whisper.

Predict the mystery

Which clue is most important?

Who was there? What did they find? Make a prediction.

No single correct prediction. Ask learners to justify their ideas using the image.
06
Reading · 6 min

Read: The Silver Box

Last Friday, Mia and Leo visited an old castle with their school group. Mia used to read mystery stories when she was younger, so she was excited. Leo didn’t use to enjoy scary stories, but he wanted to explore the castle.

As soon as they entered a small room, the lights went out. A gust of wind moved the curtains. “Did you hear that whisper?” Mia asked. Leo looked around and found a note on a table: “The silver box is not where it used to be.”

The friends felt scared, but they decided to look for clues. First, they checked behind the table. Then they heard a strange noise near the window. Leo noticed an old wooden box on the floor. Inside it was a silver box and a small map.

Just then, their teacher entered the room. She explained that the castle had a mystery game for visitors. The whisper came from a speaker, and the wind had pushed the wooden box onto the floor. Mia laughed. “That was a brilliant mystery!” she said.

🎧 Listen & follow

Use your browser’s English voice to listen to the original story.

Voice playback depends on the browser and available voices; the reading text always works offline.

Was your prediction correct? What was the real explanation?
The whisper came from a speaker; the wind moved the wooden box. The castle had a mystery game.
07
Post-reading · 6 min

Check the clues

True or false?

T, F, F, T, F. Corrections: Leo didn’t use to enjoy scary stories; the lights went out after they entered; the whisper came from a speaker.

🧩 Put the events in order

Tap ↑ and ↓ to arrange the story from first to last.

Discuss: Which clue was the most mysterious? Did the friends make a good decision?
Order: Mia and Leo entered the castle → lights went out → heard a whisper → found a silver box and a map → teacher explained the mystery.
08
Grammar in context · 8 min

THEN vs. ONE TIME

🔁 USED TO

Past habits and states.

I used to read comics.

I didn’t use to like mysteries.

⏪ PAST SIMPLE

Finished events.

I found a map yesterday.

Did you hear the noise?

Notice it · Habit or event?

1 habit, 2 event, 3 habit, 4 event, 5 habit, 6 event.

✏️ Complete the message

1 used to read; 2 heard; 3 didn’t use to like; 4 entered; 5 Did / use to play; 6 found.
09
Story sequencing · 4 min

Make the story flow

Connect events with:

whenas soon asafterthenuntil

Tell the story again

1. The friends entered the castle.
2. They heard a strange noise.
3. They looked behind the door.
4. They found the missing box.

Use at least two linking words. Then add a surprising ending.

Sample: “As soon as the friends entered the castle, they heard a strange noise. Then they looked behind the door. After that, they found the missing box.”
10
Communicative practice · 9 min

Three mystery cases

Case 1 — The Strange Whisper

Two friends heard a whisper in an empty room. Was it a gust of wind, a person or something mysterious?

Defend your theory: “I think… because…”
Challenge your partner: “But what if…?”
There is no fixed answer. Evaluate the use of clues, logical reasoning, Past Simple and interaction. Each case is intentionally open-ended.
11
Main communication · 7 min

Mystery Council

Two detectives. Two theories. One final explanation.

🕵️ Detective A

Choose a case. Give two clues. Explain your theory.

🕵️ Detective B

Ask two questions. Suggest another explanation.

🎯 Your mission

Agree on ONE explanation and tell the story together.

I think… because… · Maybe… · What happened after…? · I agree / disagree… · As soon as… · We used to…

Write your final verdict:

Model: “I think someone switched the lights off because the storm wasn’t very strong. First, the friends entered the castle. Then the lights went out. They used to enjoy mysteries, so they looked for clues.”
12
Personalisation · 4 min

My Story Profile

📚 Talk about yourself

Choose two questions and give detailed answers.

Childhood Stories

What stories did you use to enjoy?

Favourite Genre

What kind of stories do you like now? Why?

Mysterious Experience

Have you ever experienced something strange?

My Opinion

What makes a story interesting?

Encourage contrast with used to + present preferences, or a personal Past Simple anecdote.
13
Final speaking product · 6 min

Your 60-second mystery

🎙 Tell or record your story

Include: setting + characters → strange sound or missing object → three events → surprising explanation.

01:00

✨ Success checklist

Sample: “When I was younger, I used to enjoy mystery stories. Last Saturday, my friends and I visited an old house. As soon as we entered, we heard a whisper. Then the lights went out. We felt scared, but we found a note. After we opened the window, we discovered that the noise came from the wind. We laughed.”

My confidence
